head: 39a99d08
gate: HTTP/3 concurrent owner uses a short active-command receive budget instead of waiting a full idle poll for each response command

commands.h3_concurrent: zig build test-lib -Dtest-filter="HTTP/3 continuous concurrent" --summary all

benchmark.workload: weft synthetic-handshake HTTP/3 server, one loopback connection, GET / -> 200 "ok", 10k sequential and 1k x 32-stream batches

notes: The HTTP/3 owner drains handler commands only after its current QUIC receive returns. A full poll_interval therefore appeared once per startResponse and once per writeData, producing ~2x poll latency per request. Command tracing at poll_interval=1ms measured 0.92-1.00ms between submit and drain for both command kinds, while execute itself took 5-45us. command_poll_interval defaults to 100us and is used only while active handlers exist; idle connections keep poll_interval. Sequential H3 improved 8.1x to 261.6us/req. The 32-stream batch path improved much less (117us -> 128us per request); server execute and drain tracing showed ~100us per command with 5-45us execute, so the remaining batch gap is not explained by the command poll alone. The likely next targets are the client's per-request send loop or per-packet QUIC response processing; that split has not yet been isolated. HTTP/2 remains at 26.0us sequential and 14.9us per batched request.
